Privacy Policy

Gwansang (觀相) · Effective October 2, 2026

Gwansang is built to need as little of your data as possible. Almost everything it does happens on your phone. Your face reading is the one exception: your photo leaves your phone only when you ask for the reading and agree. This policy explains exactly what goes where.

What stays on your device

  • Your birth date and time, your chart, and every daily, weekly, and monthly reading. These are computed on your phone and stored in the app’s private storage. They are never sent to us or to anyone else.
  • Your settings, including the morning-reading reminder. Reminders are local notifications scheduled on your phone; no push server is involved.
  • The face photo you add, and the facial landmarks the app finds in it. The app keeps only a re-saved copy of the photo, without its location or camera details. The landmarks are found on your phone by Apple Vision (iOS) or Google ML Kit (Android), which run on the device.

On Android, Google ML Kit also sends Google basic technical information about its own use — your phone’s model and OS version, the app’s name and version, and performance and error figures — which Google uses to maintain and improve ML Kit. It never includes your photo or anything about your face.

On Android, backups and device-to-device transfers are turned off for this app. On iPhone, if you back up to iCloud, the backup may include the app’s data, protected by your Apple Account like the rest of your backup.

When you ask for your face reading

The full face reading is written and drawn by AI services, so it needs your photo to leave your phone. The app asks for your permission first, and nothing is sent until you agree. When you do, it sends:

  • Your face photo, re-saved on your phone first so it carries no location or camera details.
  • A few proportions of your face measured on your phone — ratios such as the gap between your brows against the width of your eye. These are numbers, not the positions of your features.
  • A random identifier created on your phone, and a label for the photo so that a new photo gets a new reading. Neither is linked to your name, your account, or your phone’s advertising or hardware identifiers.
  • The anonymous purchase identifier described under Purchases, so that our backend can check that the reading was paid for.

These go to our backend, run by Supabase on Amazon Web Services servers in Northern California, USA. Our backend passes your photo to Replicate, an AI platform in the United States, which runs two AI models for us: Anthropic’s Claude writes the reading, and OpenAI’s image model draws your face-chart portrait. To do that, Replicate sends your photo to Anthropic and OpenAI (and, possibly, the cloud providers that host their models).

The reading is made first. If the photo is not a single adult face, or is unsafe, no reading is made, no portrait is drawn, and neither the photo nor anything about it is kept. Only the time of the request is recorded, for the daily limits described below.

What we keep, and for how long

  • Your photo is never stored on our servers. Our backend deletes it from Replicate as soon as your reading is made (if that ever fails, Replicate removes uploaded files on its own within 24 hours).
  • Replicate automatically removes the data of each AI request after about one hour, though copies may remain in its backups for a limited time.
  • Under their published API policies, Anthropic and OpenAI do not use API data to train their models by default, and may keep it for up to 30 days to operate the service and prevent abuse — longer if a request is flagged for safety review or the law requires it.
  • The reading text and the portrait drawing are saved on your phone. Our backend keeps a copy, linked to your random identifier, for 30 days so the app can fetch them again if a download fails, and then deletes it automatically. The portrait is stored privately; the app downloads it through a link that expires within an hour.
  • To keep the service affordable and prevent abuse, we record when each reading was requested, with a scrambled (hashed) form of your random identifier and nothing else, and delete these records after 30 days. They contain no photo and no reading.
  • When you delete your face reading, we keep a scrambled form of your identifier, the time of the deletion, and the labels of the deleted photos for up to two days, so that a reading already being made at that moment is not saved afterwards.
  • If you report a reading, we keep the reason you chose, with your random identifier and the label of the reported photo, until you delete your face reading, and for at most 90 days.
  • Our hosting provider keeps standard technical logs (such as the time of a request) for security, for a short period.
  • Every service named here handles your data only to provide this feature, as our processor.

What we never do

  • We do not use your face, your photo, the measurements, or your readings to identify you, for marketing or advertising, for tracking, for data mining, or for profiling beyond the reading you asked for.
  • We do not sell or share your data with anyone other than the services named here, and only to make your reading and handle your purchases.
  • We run no analytics of our own and use no advertising identifiers and no location data. The only diagnostics are Google ML Kit’s on Android, described above.

Withdrawing consent and deleting your data

  • Settings → Delete face reading removes the reading, the portrait, and any reports from our backend, and the photo and portrait from your phone. It also withdraws your permission: the app will ask again before sending any photo. The request-time records described above, which hold no photo or reading, expire on their own.
  • Choosing a new photo replaces the old reading, and the old one is deleted.
  • Settings → Start over does the same as Delete face reading and also clears your chart and settings.
  • Deleting the app removes everything stored on your phone, and our copy is deleted automatically 30 days after the reading was made. To have it deleted sooner, use Delete face reading before you remove the app, or email us the reading reference shown in Settings → Face reading.

Purchases

Subscriptions and purchases are paid through Apple or Google. We never receive your payment details.

The app uses RevenueCat, a service in the United States, to check and keep track of purchases. RevenueCat receives a random purchase identifier it creates on your phone, what you bought and when, and basic technical details such as the app’s version and platform and your language and currency, along with your IP address, as with any internet request. It does not receive advertising identifiers, your location, your photo, your face reading, or your birth details.

Each face reading is a separate purchase. When you ask for one, our backend uses that purchase identifier to ask RevenueCat whether a face reading was bought, and records which purchase paid for which reading (the purchase’s ID and the time) so that a purchase is never spent twice. This record holds no photo and no reading. It is kept after you delete your face reading, because deleting it would make a spent purchase look unused.

Children

Gwansang is not directed at children under 13, and the face reading is for adults only. We do not knowingly collect personal information from children. If you believe a child has used the face reading, contact us and we will delete it.

Your rights

Depending on where you live, you may have the right to access, correct, delete, or object to the processing of your data. Most of this you can do in the app; for anything else, email us and we will respond within 30 days.

Changes

If this policy changes, the new version will appear in the app with a new date. If the change affects the face reading, the app will ask for your permission again before sending anything.
